history.period: Original temple 50+ years old; present structure inaugurated 20 June 2007
history.summary: The Jagannath temple of Rayagada town, known as Sradhha Shrikhetra, stands on the southern side of Rayagada. Lord Jagannath with Balabhadra and Subhadra are the main deities in a Kalinga-style complex of seven shrines (one source describes them spread across a wooded hillock). The original temple was built more than 50 years ago; the present structure was rebuilt in 2007 and inaugurated by the Gajapati Raja of Puri on 20 June 2007. Rath Yatra is the main festival, with a chariot festival celebrated like Puri's. The temple lies about 110 km from Sabara Srikhetra, Koraput (per Wikipedia). COORDINATE FLAG: Wikipedia and trek.zone list this temple's coordinates as 19.16003°N, 83.40779°E — identical to Wikipedia's coordinates for the Majhighariani Temple (seq 2488b), so one or both may be a copy-paste error; used here as the best corroborated figures available. IMAGE FLAG: the representative image comes from a Rayagada pilgrimage travelogue (Ghumakkar) and is not verified to depict this temple specifically.
